key_insight: UniTB combines physical tight-binding priors with equivariant deep learning to predict Hamiltonians across diverse chemistries while constraining unphysical band shifts.
engineering_relevance: Its fast UniTB-Flash variant supports large-cell modeling and materials screening with linear-cost prior assembly, while UniTB provides more accurate property values.
method: Learn E(3)-equivariant corrections to a physically motivated prior Hamiltonian.
Use prior-routed mixture-of-experts learning and a charge-equilibration head.
Bound band shifts through projection and accelerate computation with SO(2) GPU kernels.
evidence_signal: Trained on 29,242 crystals, UniTB achieves 0.48 meV matrix-element error on nonmagnetic test crystals spanning 68 elements; both variants agree with DFT optics and conductivity for amorphous Ge-Sb-Te without amorphous training data.
watch_item: Reported test accuracy concerns nonmagnetic crystals; applicability to magnetic materials and broader disordered chemistries requires further validation.
paper_title: Physical structure as an organizing principle for universal Hamiltonian learning
